terms.sub: Concept of Milieu Interieur and Homeostasis
clues: Walter Bradford Cannon coined this term in 1929
It represents a dynamic steady state rather than a rigid static equilibrium
It is the maintenance of nearly constant conditions in the body's internal environment

terms.sub: Concept of Milieu Interieur and Homeostasis
clues: Claude Bernard introduced this French phrase in the nineteenth century
It consists mainly of the extracellular interstitial fluid bathing tissue cells
Its constancy is what Bernard called the condition for free and independent life
Most physiological control systems in the human body rely on this mechanism
Examples include the arterial baroreceptor reflex and TSH suppression by thyroxine
It triggers an effector response that opposes and reverses an initial deviation from the set point
Unchecked, it can create a lethal vicious cycle during severe hemorrhagic shock
It drives the preovulatory LH surge and the upstroke of an action potential
It amplifies an initial change in the same direction until a discrete event like childbirth ends it
Seeing or smelling food triggers cephalic-phase insulin secretion through this mechanism
It accounts for the immediate jump in ventilation at the very start of exercise
It initiates anticipatory corrective actions before a regulated variable actually changes

terms.sub: Components of a Homeostatic Control System
clues: Pyrogens raise this hypothalamic reference value during the onset of fever
Baroreceptors can reset this value upward in chronic untreated hypertension
It is the target reference value around which a homeostatic variable is regulated
Histamine and nitric oxide commonly act through this local mode of communication
The chemical messenger diffuses through interstitial fluid without entering the blood
A cell releases a signal that acts exclusively on neighboring target cells
It is entrained by light hitting the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus
Plasma cortisol peaks in the early morning and troughs at night following this pattern
It is an endogenous biological oscillation repeating roughly every 24 hours
